mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, with t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero mean return.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% over two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces inflationary pressure and increases the likelihood of future monetary easing, thereby boosting equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered instances, or the average return is less than 0.5% in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts below 1700 thousand units in two consecutive months signals a contraction in consumer durable spending and residential investment, which triggers a reassessment of corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered instances, or the return distribution has a mean above -0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and a rise in the unemployment rate indicates a supply-side contraction coupled with weak labor demand, signaling an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 104.0 and UNRATE > 3.8% in same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and UNRATE meet the trigger condition, or the joint signal fails to outperform a single-series benchmark in walk-forward IC tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the CPIAUCSL above 288.0 with a 12-month growth rate exceeding 3.5% signals entrenched inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in high-inflation periods, or the average return exceeds -1.0% in such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 660,000 million dollars combined with a rising GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates strong aggregate demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS and GDPC1 exceed thresholds, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 thousand in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals robust labor market strength that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger, or the signal fails to generate a positive average return in 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 104.0 for two consecutive months, coupled with a rising unemployment rate, indicates a contraction in manufacturing output and weakening labor demand, which signals an impending economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 104.0 for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE > 3.7%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered instances, or the average return exceeds -1.5% in such periods.
